summary.primary_finding: Model produces statistically supported predictive edge over pre-game market consensus for the trigger-state subpopulation.

calibration_not_ranking.interpretation: The model wins by probability-level trigger-state adjustment, not by ranking teams better than the pre-game market.

deficit_pattern.interpretation: Brier improvement increases monotonically with deficit, the expected signature of useful in-game-state information.

tertiary_betting_context.interpretation: The tested favorite-side policy failed in hindsight; this does not contradict predictive improvement over stale pre-game probabilities.

summary.project_conclusion: Predictive edge versus pre-game market consensus is validated. Live-line betting edge remains untested and requires future live market data collection.

data_provenance.line_timestamp_caveat: CFBD /lines cache has game startDate but no provider-level line timestamp. Cached spread/moneyline fields are treated as latest available pre-game lines.

provider_policy.direction_conflict_definition: moneyline-implied favorite side (negative moneyline, or raw implied probability > 0.5 when one-sided) differs from spread-implied favorite side (negative spread)
provider_policy.direction_conflict_policy: exclude conflicting providers; if no direction-consistent moneyline remains, use spread conversion
